newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea to reopen embassy in Algeria.
newsitem.headline: South Korea to reopen embassy in Algeria.

text.p: South Korea plans to reopen its embassy in Algeria which it had closed in 1994 because of the worsening political situation there, a foreign ministry spokesman said on Friday.
"The government plans to restore the Algerian embassy, which had been tentatively shut down, from October 1," the spokesman said in a statement.
It said South Korea would appoint an ambassador to Algeria as soon as the political situation in the country stabilises.

South Korea withdrew its diplomats in 1994 after Kang Dae-hyun, a senior local representative of South Korea's Daewoo Group was gunned down by Moslem fundamentalists near his home outside Algiers on October 12, 1994.
Daewoo has invested in a hotel construction project and a Korean consortium led by state-funded Korea Petroleum Development Corp is exploiting two oil block in Algeria.
